title: Farfalle Estive
subtitle: Cold summer pasta with fresh tomatoes, mozzarella, basil, and olive oil
excerpt: Farfalle estive is a cold summer pasta dressed with fresh tomatoes, torn mozzarella, basil, and olive oil. The pasta is cooked and cooled, then tossed with the raw ingredients just before serving. It is a salad as much as a pasta dish, and it requires ripe tomatoes and good olive oil to work.
sourceNotes: Cold pasta dressed with fresh tomatoes and mozzarella is a summer tradition throughout central and southern Italy, particularly in Lazio and Campania. The Caprese combination of tomato, mozzarella, and basil applied to pasta is a natural extension of the classic salad.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales well. Dress in batches so each serving gets fresh tomatoes and oil.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook and cool the pasta up to 4 hours ahead and store loosely oiled in the fridge. Add the remaining ingredients just before serving.

content.text: Farfalle estive is a cold summer pasta. Farfalle is tossed with ripe tomatoes, torn mozzarella, fresh basil, and extra virgin olive oil. The dish only works in summer, when tomatoes are ripe enough to give juice. Out-of-season tomatoes produce a flat result. Dress the pasta 10 to 15 minutes before serving to let the flavours settle.

items.prepNote: buffalo or fior di latte, torn

content.text: Cook the farfalle in generously salted boiling water until fully al dente: 1 minute longer than you would for a hot dish. Drain and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking and prevent sticking. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil and spread on a tray to cool to room temperature.

Rub the inside of a large serving bowl with the cut garlic if using. Add the chopped tomatoes, season generously with salt and a grind of pepper, and toss with the remaining olive oil. Leave for 5 minutes: the tomatoes will release some juice.
Add the cooled farfalle, torn mozzarella, torn basil, and olives if using. Toss to combine. Taste and adjust seasoning. Let the pasta sit for 10 to 15 minutes at room temperature before serving.

items.symptom: Pasta is gluey and clumped together
items.cause: Not rinsed and oiled promptly after draining
items.fix: For cold pasta, rinsing and oiling immediately after cooking is essential. It is the one case where rinsing pasta is correct: otherwise the starch sets and the farfalle stick together.

items.symptom: Mozzarella is watery and dilutes the dressing
items.cause: Mozzarella released whey into the pasta
items.fix: Drain the mozzarella for 20 minutes on kitchen paper before tearing it in. Buffalo mozzarella is wetter than fior di latte: drain it longer.
This dish depends on ripe summer tomatoes. Out of season, use good cherry tomatoes rather than large varieties. Season the tomatoes aggressively: they need more salt than you think.

content.text: Cold dressed pasta is a summer tradition across Italy. It is eaten for lunch or as part of a cold spread. The Caprese elements of tomato, mozzarella, and basil are used here in the same spirit as the Capri salad, but with pasta to make a more filling dish. In Italy it is common picnic and beach food, often made the night before.
